task.title: M8: Extracted boundary edges, starting with HTTP routes between Go handlers and TS fetch calls
task.description:
The import graph stops at the language boundary: workbook is Go on the server and TypeScript on the client and no edge crosses between them. Add a new edge kind 'route' extracted by matching HTTP route registrations in Go (net/http HandleFunc, mux/chi/echo/gin-style Method+path registrations with string-literal paths) against request sites in TypeScript (fetch, axios, and string literals that look like paths passed to a request helper). Matching is on the path template after normalizing parameter segments (:id, {id}, [id], and template-literal ${} all become a wildcard). Edges run from the calling TS file to the Go handler file (or Go package module at module level) and carry the method and path as metadata. Extend the Snapshot edge type with kind: 'route' and keep existing consumers unaffected. Cycle detection ignores route edges. This is the first of a family (queues, RPC, schema) so keep the extractor interface general: an extractor produces {file, line, kind:'provides'|'consumes', key} rows and the matcher joins provides to consumes by key.

Acceptance criteria:
- Analyzing workbook produces at least one route edge for each API endpoint the web UI calls; codeviz analyze --json reports the count of route edges and the number of unmatched provides and consumes.
- Route edges render in the Graph and Map views in a distinguishable style (dashed, own color) and can be toggled off independently of import edges.
- Compare view shows added and removed route edges with the same green/red treatment as import edges.
- Parameterized paths match (/api/snapshots/:sha matches fetch(`/api/snapshots/${sha}`)); differing methods on the same path produce separate edges.
- No new runtime dependencies; extraction uses the existing tree-sitter TS and Go trees. One fixture-based test with a two-file Go+TS pair.
